commits.subject: ui: pdf - lines outside a path are stroked or ended in their own record
commits.body:
TPdfCanvas.NewPath set fNewPath. Only the EMF enumeration reads that
flag, and there it means "a GDI path is being recorded". So every n
outside a path left the enumeration as if inside one:
- POLYLINETO wrote its own n first, so a PolylineTo outside a path was
  never stroked.
- After a Polyline of a null pen, a line drawn with a pen had no S, and
  without a MoveTo no m either. A later shape painted it with its own
  fill, and without one the line was lost. The pen's w and RG landed
  inside the open path.

Also fixed:
- LineTo and ArcTo of a null pen left their geometry open, and the next
  shape stroked it in the colour of before.
- Arc of a null pen was stroked at once.
- A LineTo of a pen was stroked at once but stayed pending (fInlined), so
  the next shape, pen change or transform wrote a lone S.

The flag now belongs to the path bracket. PathBegin sets it and
PathClose clears it; TPdfCanvas.NewPath only writes n. Outside a path,
LINETO, ARCTO and ARC stroke with a pen or end with n, as the other line
records do. Nothing is left pending any more, so fInlined and its
consumers are gone. The resets that only undid NewPath's side effect are
removed, including FillRectangle's ResetNewPath parameter, and so is the
leading n of POLYLINETO.

Tests:
- EmfNullPenLines (6 checks)
- EmfLineAfterEndedPath (24 checks), six cases: PolylineTo of a pen and
  of a null pen; a line after a null-pen Polyline, after FillRgn and
  after PolyPolyline; PolylineTo in a path.
On master's sources, 11 checks fail. The polyline case selects a brush
here, since this renderer leaves out a polyline of no pen nor brush.

MetafileRenderingAndOrientation loses 406 S lines and nothing else; 405
of them followed another S. The Delphi hash is now $439DB6C2. The length
check moves from 6500 to 6400: the PDF went from 6522 to 6468 bytes.
FPC 3.2.2 Win32 keeps its known failure there (6433 before, 6370 now).

Results:
- Delphi 13 Win32 and Delphi 7: 217
- Delphi 13 Win64, FPC 3.3.1 and FPC 3.2.2 Win64: 214
- FPC 3.2.2 Win32: the known MetafileRenderingAndOrientation #3

This is the same change as in our engine
(martin-doyle/mORMot2-PDF-CrossPlatform#98).

Reviewed with Codex.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: test: pdf - the metafile checks expect a 96 DPI screen on any screen
commits.body:
A test program that is DPI-aware sees the real screen DPI, as a Delphi
manifest makes it. On a scaled screen, TPdfDocument then maps the metafile
pixels with 72/144 instead of 72/96. Found at 150 % scaling (144 DPI):
- EmfClipRestoreDC #12 and #18 (from #688) missed their coordinates.
- The MetafileRenderingAndOrientation hash was $332DBFD7 on Delphi.
- Its length check failed on FPC.

RenderedEmf and the first document of MetafileRenderingAndOrientation now
set ScreenLogPixels to 96, so the checks hold on any screen. A program that
is not DPI-aware already got 96, so its output is unchanged.

TTestUiPdf run DPI-aware at 144 DPI: 3 failures before, none after.
Delphi 13 Win32 gave 187 checks and FPC 3.3.1 gave 184.

Normal runs:
- Delphi 13 Win32 and Delphi 7: 187
- Delphi 13 Win64, FPC 3.3.1 and FPC 3.2.2 Win64: 184
- FPC 3.2.2 Win32: its known MetafileRenderingAndOrientation #3, as on
  master

Found while checking the EmfPlus* failures reported in #690. Those came
from a mix of old and new units.

Reviewed with Codex.
commits.author: Sven Harazim
